purpose: Research-only handoff for nums 746-765 in data-mcudc.js. Built from live Common Sense Media refetches of catalog srcUrl pages. Do not treat as production data until reviewed and transformed through the official workflow.

contentFlagModel.mappingNote: This refetch preserves CSM's current visible category label and proposes the nearest app level. Production catalog edits should be made only by the follow-up importer/reviewer.

entries.title: Avengers: Age of Ultron

violence.summary: Relentless superhero destruction includes gunfire, deaths, flying cars, collapsing buildings, missiles, children in danger, mass civilian peril, and one especially sad death.

language.summary: Moderate profanity, insults, and religious exclamations appear, including an early swear that is immediately called out.

romance.summary: Couples kiss and flirt, with brief sexual banter but no explicit sexual activity or nudity.

drinking.summary: Only brief social or celebratory drinking is noted.

handoffNotes: A notable character death may need emotional-context prose for sensitive viewers.

entries.title: Batman vs. Robin

violence.summary: Frequent animated combat includes shootings, rifle use, parental murder flashbacks, child abuse, a child killing an owl, kidnapped children in cages, and frightening Dollmaker imagery.

language.summary: Occasional mild-to-moderate profanity and insults are used.

romance.summary: Sex is implied after a bedroom scene, and there is innuendo involving Bruce, Nightwing, and their romantic partners.

drinking.summary: Adults drink wine and liquor without drunken behavior, and Batman is drugged with a hallucinogen that causes disturbing visions.

handoffNotes: Child captivity, child abuse, and Bruce's parental-murder trauma may need prose treatment beyond the numeric violence flag.

entries.title: Fantastic Four

violence.summary: Sci-fi violence turns graphic near the end, with many deaths, blood, exploding heads, the Thing used as a military weapon, intense transformations, and a sibling beating.

language.summary: A few moderate swears and crude terms appear.

romance.summary: Only flirting and loaded looks are flagged, without actual romance or sex.

drinking.summary: Young adult characters drink heavily enough to make poor decisions.

handoffNotes: CSM labels Drinking, Drugs & Smoking as 'a little' while the detail describes heavy drinking that leads to bad decisions.

violence.summary: Dark superhero violence includes shootings, explosions, blood, demonic imagery, neck biting, police battles, and a woman killed by a sword through the chest.

language.summary: Occasional profanity includes moderate swears, crude words, insults, and religious exclamations.

romance.summary: Innuendo, revealing superhero costuming, and visible female android nudity are flagged.

drinking.summary: A college flashback includes marijuana references and characters seeming high after a party, plus pipe smoking.

entries.title: Justice League: Throne of Atlantis

violence.summary: Animated action includes a prolonged bar fight, club beatings, two stabbing deaths, a shark killing, monster-mask imagery, machine guns, and rocket launchers.

language.summary: Occasional profanity includes moderate swears and insults.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface a meaningful sex, romance, or nudity concern.

drinking.summary: Arthur is severely intoxicated in a dive bar, starts a fight while drinking, and is shown hung over the next day.

handoffNotes: Arthur's grief after his father's death and later maternal loss may need emotional-context prose.

entries.title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice

violence.summary: Dark superhero violence includes assassinations, execution-style shootings, an explosive room attack, abductions at gunpoint, a deadly car chase, collapsing buildings, injured crowds, and Batman and Superman badly hurting each other.

language.summary: Language is limited but includes a couple of moderate swears.

romance.summary: Clark and Lois kiss passionately, including a bath scene with partial nudity; Bruce wakes beside a partially nude woman and flirts with Diana.

drinking.summary: Bruce drinks wine frequently, and adults drink cocktails at parties.

handoffNotes: CSM notes this review covers the PG-13 theatrical release; the R-rated extended cut may differ.

entries.title: Batman: Bad Blood

violence.summary: Most of the film is animated mayhem: explosions, collapsing buildings, gunfights, fistfights, swordplay, torture, landslides, stabbing, beheading, apparent hero deaths, and glimpsed family deaths.

language.summary: Some mild-to-moderate swearing and insults are used, occasionally by Robin.

romance.summary: A brief sexual fantasy involves shirtless Batman and multiple women, and Batwoman's dating life and potential new romantic interest are referenced.

drinking.summary: Background social drinking appears, Kate Kane's past heavy drinking is mentioned, and one character secretly drinks from a flask.

handoffNotes: Batwoman's past substance-abuse history may need prose context if the app distinguishes current use from backstory.

entries.title: Captain America: Civil War

violence.summary: Avengers fight enemies and each other with weapons and powers, alongside explosions, gunfire, collateral casualties, serious injuries, grief after a death, and a disturbing past killing.

language.summary: Infrequent but moderate swearing, insults, and religious exclamations appear.

romance.summary: Romance is limited to a quick kiss, longing looks, and a few embraces.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a drinking, drugs, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: The grief thread, teammate-on-teammate conflict, and revealed past killing may need prose beyond the violence level.

violence.summary: Fantasy action includes large-scale destruction, martial arts with magical weapons, surgery and bloody injuries, a brutal texting-related car crash, a fall through glass, a non-gory beheading, and nightmarish imagery.

language.summary: A small number of moderate swears and crude insults are used.

romance.summary: A past intimate relationship is discussed, including a brief reference to sleeping together.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a drinking, drugs, or smoking concern.

entries.title: Justice League vs. Teen Titans

violence.summary: Animated violence and demonic imagery run throughout, with sword fighting, a decapitation, electrocution, explosions, punches, kicks, and characters violently thrown around.

language.summary: Only a few mild profanities are noted.

romance.summary: Starfire appears in a revealing robe, and dialogue includes sexual innuendo about Raven's parents and teen hookups.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a drinking, drugs, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: Demonic possession and Raven's family backstory may need prose context for sensitive viewers.

entries.title: Suicide Squad

violence.summary: Violence includes executions, shootings, supernatural instant kills, fire attacks, military weapons, explosions, deaths or presumed deaths, widespread destruction, and a remembered family tragedy.

language.summary: Several moderate swears, crude sexual terms, insults, and possibly one stronger profanity are used.

romance.summary: Harley is heavily sexualized through outfits, dancing, and club scenes; there are passionate kisses, references to sleeping together, and crude comments.

drinking.summary: The squad drinks together in a bar, and adults drink at the Joker's club.

handoffNotes: Sexist abuse and Diablo's family tragedy may need prose treatment outside the four category levels.

entries.title: X-Men: Apocalypse

violence.summary: Large-scale superhero violence includes weapons, explosions, flying bodies, global destruction threats, a near-instant head-destruction sequence, bloody Wolverine slashing, and a child's death with grief.

language.summary: Language includes one F-word plus moderate profanity, mild swears, and religious exclamations.

romance.summary: There is flirting, revealing costuming on some female characters, and Mystique's body-armored natural form.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a drinking, drugs, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: The death of Magneto's family, including a child, should stay in emotional/sad-content prose.

entries.title: Batman and Harley Quinn

violence.summary: Comic-book action includes monster killings, a giant spike through a chest, machine guns, handguns, martial arts fighting, pratfalls, and Harley breaking the arm of someone who grabs her.

language.summary: Mild profanity mixes with crude sexual wordplay, obscene gestures, middle-finger use, and a graphic gag caption during a fight.

romance.summary: This has unusually adult sexual content for animated Batman, including Harley in underwear, implied sex with Nightwing, an erection reference, vibrator innuendo, sexual dancing, and objectifying comments.

drinking.summary: A bar scene includes drinking.

handoffNotes: CSM labels Violence & Scariness as 'some' though details include fatal monster attacks and a spike-through-chest death; reviewer may want to compare against other animated DC entries.

entries.title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2

violence.summary: Space action includes guns, swords, taser-like weapons, crashes, explosions, warlike ship battles, huge enemies, executions by airlock, high body counts, bloody arrow kills, planet-level destruction, and a major death.

language.summary: Language is not constant but includes moderate swears, crude insults, and frequent euphemistic name-calling.

romance.summary: Romantic tension, scantily clad human-like robots, near kisses, conception references, and flirtation about natural reproduction are flagged.

drinking.summary: Ravagers and others drink in pub and ship settings, some to visible drunkenness, and Groot is doused with alcohol.

handoffNotes: A popular character's death and chosen-family themes may need emotional-context prose.

entries.title: Justice League

violence.summary: Large superhero battles include explosions, widespread destruction, many weapons, monster attacks with green blood, a resurrected Superman injuring Batman, and a family nearly killed.

language.summary: A few stronger swears, bleeped F-words, religious exclamations, and insults appear.

romance.summary: Content is limited to shirtless male characters, a reunited couple kissing and embracing, and comments about Wonder Woman's attractiveness.

drinking.summary: Adults drink in pubs and privately, Aquaman downs liquor, and Bruce and Diana share a drink.

handoffNotes: CSM notes the review reflects the original theatrical release, not the longer extended cut.

entries.title: Teen Titans: The Judas Contract

violence.summary: Near-continuous animated violence includes lasers, guns, swords, fire, arrows, wild animals, point-blank shootings, stabbing, torture, crushing, captivity, restraints, blood, and deaths.

language.summary: Occasional moderate profanity and insults are used.

romance.summary: Kissing, embracing, mild seduction, revealing outfits, emphasized breasts, and light sexual banter appear.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface a drinking, drugs, or smoking concern.

handoffNotes: Betrayal and a team member's eventual amends may need prose context if emotional themes are tracked.

entries.title: The Lego Batman Movie

violence.summary: Constant toy-brick action includes bad guys, attacks, crashes, explosions, bombs, guns, fire, lava, crumbling Gotham scenes, and ongoing peril, but no gore or lasting damage.

language.summary: Insult and potty words, mild exclamations, British slang, and jokes about Dick/Robin's name appear.

romance.summary: Very mild flirting, Batman admiring Barbara and his own physique, underwear or robe moments, Robin's pants-free costume gag, and over-kids'-heads name jokes are flagged.

drinking.summary: Only a reference to Alfred drinking wine and unclear party beverages are mentioned.

handoffNotes: CSM shows the category as Drinking, Drugs & Smoking 'none' even though the detail text mentions a wine reference; level 1 is retained.

entries.title: Thor: Ragnarok

violence.summary: Comic-book violence includes explosions, battles, firearms, fantasy weapons, many deaths, scary Hela scenes, slashing and stabbing, a melting death, and a bloody wound visible across multiple scenes.

language.summary: Moderate swearing appears along with extended crude body-part humor.

romance.summary: Brief nonsexual Hulk rear nudity and references to masturbation and orgies are noted without explicit detail.

drinking.summary: Valkyrie drinks heavily as part of a trauma backstory without real consequences, and other characters drink socially.

handoffNotes: Major traumatic change, Valkyrie's trauma-linked drinking, and Asgard's destruction may need prose context.

entries.title: Wonder Woman

violence.summary: World War I and superhero action include frequent battles, arrows, swords, guns, high body counts, poison gas killing officials, planned gas warfare, collateral damage, and several sad deaths.

language.summary: Language is mild and limited to light profanity, religious exclamations, and insults.

romance.summary: Romance includes innuendo, reproduction and pleasure references, Steve covering his nudity after a bath, passionate kissing, implied possible overnight intimacy, revealing armor, and one underwear gag.

drinking.summary: Characters drink beer or champagne in pubs and receptions, and one character gets drunk and fights.

handoffNotes: CSM labels Violence & Scariness as 'some' despite frequent war violence, high body counts, poison gas, and multiple emotionally heavy deaths.
Steve's sacrifice and other sad deaths should remain in emotional/sad-content prose.

entries.title: Ant-Man and the Wasp

violence.summary: Frequent but lighter Marvel action includes chases, peril, crashes, property destruction, fights with guns and knives, a missile countdown, a woman used as a weapon, giant-ant attacks, and painful parental-loss flashbacks.

language.summary: Moderate profanity, crude words, religious exclamations, and insults appear.

romance.summary: Established couples kiss briefly, there is some flirting, and Scott is shirtless in a bath scene.

drinking.summary: Adults drink wine with a meal, and Hope drugs Scott to move him against his will.

handoffNotes: Flashbacks with children losing parents and Ava's chronic pain/mortal danger may need emotional prose.
Drugging Scott is non-recreational but should remain in the drinking/drugs summary.
